title: Per-subtoken SLA budgeting and cache-penalty instrumentation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: provide a production-ready, auditable per-subtoken timing ledger that attributes SLA budget and cost impact across cache hits/misses. Deliverables: (1) lightweight per-subtoken timing probe injected at the serving runtime tracing hooks, (2) aggregation rules that separate user-visible emission time vs. cache penalty time, (3) a pipeline that emits both high-cardinality micro-ledger metrics and rollup counters into the metrics/log ingestion system, and (4) dashboards and a small alerting surface for SLA regressions. Motivation: current coarse request-level latency blurs cache hit penalties with emission cost leading to incorrect cost allocation and noisy SLA alerts. This work aims to make attribution explicit so product teams can tune caching, batching and quantization with accurate unit economics.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-subtoken probe spans with stable schema (span_type=subtoken, fields: request_id, seq_index, phase=[emit|cache_lookup|cache_apply], elapsed_ms)
Aggregation job produces daily and hourly rollups that reconcile to existing per-request latency totals within 1% on average
Cache-penalty allocation algorithm documented and implemented (configurable weights) and validated on synthetic workloads with known cache hit distributions
Grafana dashboard: per-model SLA budget burn-down, cache-penalty heatmap, and top-10 requests by attributed cost available in console-ops namespace
End-to-end pipeline under accepted ingestion cost threshold (adds <5% to ingestion volume for standard 99th-percentile workloads)
